alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 8 at 12:34AM CST until November 9 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south Texas, including the following areas,
Aransas Islands, Bee, Coastal Aransas, Coastal Kleberg, Coastal
Nueces, Coastal Refugio, Coastal San Patricio, Duval, Goliad,
Inland Kleberg, Inland Nueces, Inland Refugio, Inland San Patricio,
Jim Wells, Kleberg Islands, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen, Nueces
Islands and Webb.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread forecast rainfall amounts of 2-5 inches will be common
across South Texas. Isolated amounts of 7 to 9 inches remains a
possibility, especially in the vicinity of training and slow
moving storms. While soils will be able to absorb most of this
moisture, the higher rainfall rates, slow storm motion, and
training can quickly lead to localized, urban flooding and in
locations with poor drainage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 8 at 1:23PM CST until November 8 at 4:30PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
alerts.description:
FFWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Duval County in south central Texas...
Southwestern Jim Wells County in south central Texas...
Western Kleberg County in south central Texas...

* Until 430 PM CST.

* At 123 PM CST, local law enforcement reported flash flooding on
Highways 141 and also 281 in Kleberg county. Between 5 and 8 inches
of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no
additional rainfall is occurring. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Kingsville, Premont, Ricardo, Kingsville Naval Air Station,
Riviera, La Gloria and Loyola Beach.

This includes the following highways...
US Highway 281 between mile markers 688 and 706. US Highway 77
between mile markers 690 and 708.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Ebanito Creek, Derramadero de Machos, Paisano Creek, San Fernando
Creek, Lagunas Negras, Jaboncillos Creek, Ramada del Toro Creek,
Tranquitas Creek, Baffin Bay, Salado Creek, Chiltipin Creek, Las
Animas Creek, Araa Creek, Escondido Creek, Cibolo Creek and Olmos
Creek, Los.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 8 at 12:48PM CST until November 8 at 3:45PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Cameron County in deep south Texas...
Southeastern Willacy County in deep south Texas...

* WHEN...Until 345 PM CST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable. It will
take several hours for all the water from these storms to work
through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1248 PM CST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Harlingen, San Benito, Los Fresnos, South Padre Island, Rancho
Viejo, Rio Hondo, Laureles, Arroyo City, Port Of Brownsville,
Olmito, Cameron Park, Southmost, Downtown Brownsville, La Paloma,
Brownsville, Lincoln Park, Holly Beach, Laguna Vista Police
Department, Palmer Laasko Elementary and Los Fresnos High School.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.areaDesc: Cameron, TX; Willacy, TX

alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 8 at 1:07AM CST until November 9 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous
rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, from noon CST today
through late tonight. For the High Rip Current Risk, from noon
CST today through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could
be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide at
452 PM this afternoon.
alerts.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 8:12AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Excessive rainfall is forecast to continue upstream of Los Olmos
into early this week, leading to a rise in river levels that may
approach action stage late tonight.

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...From this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground.

At 9.0 feet, Flow is high enough to close FM 1418 as water is
covering the bridge.

At 10.0 feet, Flow escapes from the Los Olmos drainage into the Palo
Blanco drainage area.

At 11.0 feet, Minor flooding with lowland flooding 300 feet wide into
the flood plain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM CST Sunday the stage was 1.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.7 feet
early Tuesday morning.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet. The river is expected to reach action
stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 8 at 12:34AM CST until November 9 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south Texas, including the following areas,
Aransas Islands, Bee, Coastal Aransas, Coastal Kleberg, Coastal
Nueces, Coastal Refugio, Coastal San Patricio, Duval, Goliad,
Inland Kleberg, Inland Nueces, Inland Refugio, Inland San Patricio,
Jim Wells, Kleberg Islands, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen, Nueces
Islands and Webb.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread forecast rainfall amounts of 2-5 inches will be common
across South Texas. Isolated amounts of 7 to 9 inches remains a
possibility, especially in the vicinity of training and slow
moving storms. While soils will be able to absorb most of this
moisture, the higher rainfall rates, slow storm motion, and
training can quickly lead to localized, urban flooding and in
locations with poor drainage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
